chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Inculcate your children with the soil of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for it is a protection.'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.تُرْبَةِ: Soil/earth (specifically referring to the sacred soil of Karbala)
key_terms.حَنِّكُوا: Inculcate or instill (literally: make sweet by placing something sweet in the mouth)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of using the soil of Imam al-Husayn for children?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes the practice of *hanak* (gently rubbing clay on a newborn's palate) using the soil of Karbala, identifying it as a spiritual *aman* (protection or safeguard). This practice underscores the Shia belief in the metaphysical efficacy of the earth of Imam al-Husayn, linking the physical act of blessing a child to the enduring spiritual legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt and their victory over tribulation.
